findings.mod_behavior: After 3 s unsuccessful native acquisition, terrain-visible fallback sets fixed=true with selected.id=0 and selected_type=3. The native publisher marks a fixed point valid. AG_Radar_System ignores that type when selecting display mode: GMT becomes GMTT (SEA becomes SEAT), but F22_AG_FIXED_TRACK is asserted only in MAP mode. A terrain point can therefore appear as a track with zero speed rather than a disclosed fallback.

findings.mod_behavior: The shared radar STT contract permits age up to 0.5 s, while Gun_Director resets beyond 0.15 s and also waits for consistent motion/current native solution. Gun_Funnel invalidates whenever F22_RADAR_STT_VALID is true, and the HUD gates it on no gun target. Thus a retained-valid STT can suppress the funnel while the tracked director is unavailable; HUD shows GUN NO SOLUTION rather than a nontracked reference. This also occurs during some lock/identity transitions and outside the director's chosen range.
findings.differences: The honest no-solution indication is a positive. However, presentation handover follows radar-lock existence rather than gun-solution availability and does not reproduce the Viper coexistence/reversion concept. The exact F-22 fallback cannot be inferred from either legacy aircraft.
findings.proposed_target: Define lock-without-solution as an explicit presentation state. Preserve an appropriate noncomputed boresight/reference, or deliberately adopt the Viper funnel coexistence rule, without pretending it is a tracked solution. Keep stricter gun-solution age gates if justified; do not simply freshen or extrapolate invalid lead data.

findings.mod_behavior: All own pilot-warning voice can be muted or reduced to zero, including urgent terrain speech. findings.differences: The global own-voice inhibit capability agrees with the stated Viper option. The separate chosen general design target for persistent suppression awareness is reduced outside AUDIO. Neither establishes an F-22 mute defect or mandatory critical-message exception.
findings.proposed_target: Choose the voice-inhibit/volume policy explicitly. Global voice inhibit is a documented Viper-like option and should not be called an F-22 defect merely because it suppresses urgent speech. Retained suppression awareness, rearm controls and any separation of critical/nonessential audio are optional design decisions; exact F-22 controls remain unresolved.
